description: SAML attacker-signed assertion should be rejected when connector is configured with CA-based signature validation (no insecureSkipSignatureValidation).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify SAML assertion signatures against the configured trust anchor (CA/caData) and must not accept attacker-signed assertions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAMLResponse even though CA-based signature validation was configured (trust anchor substitution / missing signature validation).

description: Issuer mismatch: with ssoIssuer pinned, a forged assertion with wrong Issuer should be rejected; include a control login with correct issuer first.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the configured IdP issuer (ssoIssuer) and reject assertions whose Issuer does not match the pinned issuer, even if otherwise well-formed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login with correct pinned issuer failed; cannot distinguish issuer enforcement from broken connector/SP-initiated flow.
Dex accepted a SAML assertion with an Issuer that does not match the configured ssoIssuer (issuer not bound to verification policy).

description: Config change + re-auth: demonstrate that enabling insecureSkipSignatureValidation causes attacker-signed assertions to be accepted (expected by config), then ensure secure config rejects the same forged proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Under secure configuration, Dex must reject attacker-signed assertions; acceptance should only occur when explicitly configured to skip signature validation. This sequence checks for accidental insecure-default behavior or config not taking effect.

oracle_checks.violation_description: With insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true, forged SAMLResponse was not accepted; indicates test harness/config did not take effect (cannot evaluate I1 secure-path).
After switching to secure CA-based validation, Dex still accepted an attacker-signed SAMLResponse (signature verification not applied to consumed proof).

description: I1/I3-adjacent proof-context confusion: attempt to splice RelayState from victim's SP-initiated flow with attacker's forged SAMLResponse to see if Dex verifies/consumes mismatched semantic proof context.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind signature verification and assertion consumption to the exact SP-initiated request context (RelayState/InResponseTo). A forged response must not be accepted when paired with a different session's RelayState.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a forged SAMLResponse when paired with a different session's RelayState, indicating verification/consumption context confusion (proof integrity not bound to intended request).

description: I1 semantic-proof mismatch: forge assertion where NameID (principal key) is attacker but email claim is victim; check whether Dex consumes victim email as subject despite verifying attacker NameID proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must consume the same semantic identity it verifies. If NameID is the verified principal key, downstream subject must not switch to email/username claims from the assertion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex appears to consume a different semantic identity than it verifies (e.g., switching subject binding based on email claim). Secure behavior is rejection or stable mapping to the NameID-bound identity.

description: I1 proof-integrity check: if the SAML connector is (mis)configured with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true, Dex may accept an attacker-signed SAMLResponse. Control: same forged assertion should be rejected when signature validation is enforced via caData.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the SAML proof under the intended trust policy (pinned CA) and must not accept attacker-signed assertions when signature validation is enabled; acceptance indicates verification is not applied to the consumed proof semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAMLResponse even though proof integrity should require signature validation; indicates verification policy not applied to consumed proof.
Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAMLResponse even with CA-based signature validation configured; indicates signature verification is bypassed or applied to different semantic content than consumed.
Dex produced a valid downstream session after accepting attacker-signed SAMLResponse under insecure configuration; indicates consumed proof created a session without proper integrity guarantees.

description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: submit the exact same OneTimeUse assertion twice (same Assertion/@ID). Second attempt must be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion marked with <OneTimeUse/> must not be accepted more than once; replay of the same assertion ID should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control OneTimeUse assertion was rejected; cannot evaluate replay enforcement.
SP accepted replayed SAML assertion with <OneTimeUse/> (same Assertion/@ID used twice).

description: Replay the exact same SAML assertion ID after revoking the first session to see if Dex incorrectly ties replay protection to active sessions only (should be global/stateful).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion (by Assertion/@ID) must be one-time and must not be accepted again even if the prior session is revoked.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial SAML login/token exchange did not succeed, so replay result is inconclusive.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion ID after session revocation; replay protection may be incorrectly scoped to active sessions.

description: Attempt an expired assertion first (should be rejected), then reuse the same Assertion/@ID with a valid time window to see if Dex incorrectly 'burns' or mishandles assertion IDs across failed validations (freshness state confusion). Includes a second identity as a control.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Expired assertions must be rejected, and assertion ID tracking must not allow a previously-seen ID to be accepted later (even if earlier attempt was expired).

params.saml_response: FORGE(target_identity=attackerB, email=attackerB@example.com, provider=dex, realm=default, fixed_assertion_id=_expired_then_valid, expired_assertion=true)

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); assertion lifetime not enforced.

Dex accepted a SAML assertion with an Assertion/@ID that was already used in a prior attempt (even if that attempt was expired); assertion ID replay tracking may be bypassable via failed-validation priming.
Control failed: second identity could not complete SAML login/userinfo; environment/connector may be misconfigured.

description: Control valid login, then attempt an expired assertion twice with the same Assertion/@ID. First expired attempt should be rejected; second should also be rejected (no acceptance and no state confusion that 'un-expired' or bypasses checks on replay). Includes a second identity control to ensure connector still works.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Expired SAML assertions must be rejected consistently, and replaying the same expired assertion must not be accepted due to cache/state confusion.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_control_valid_login_status < 400 AND user_attacker_expired_first_login_status >= 400 AND user_attacker_expired_replay_login_status >= 400 AND user_second_control_valid_login_status < 400
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (or accepted it on replay), indicating missing NotOnOrAfter enforcement or state confusion in freshness checks.

description: Replay the same SAML assertion ID after a connector re-provision (config change + re-auth). Replay protection should not be lost across connector lifecycle changes; second acceptance indicates replay cache is not persisted or is reset unsafely.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Replay protection for SAML assertion IDs should remain effective across connector reconfiguration/re-provisioning; a previously accepted assertion must not become reusable after config changes.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a previously used SAML Assertion/@ID after connector re-provisioning; replay cache/state appears reset or not persisted, enabling reuse of one-time artifacts.

description: SAML freshness: ensure a failed validation attempt does not 'reset' or otherwise allow later reuse of the same Assertion/@ID. Attack: submit an expired assertion with a fixed Assertion ID (expected reject), then submit a valid assertion reusing the same Assertion ID (must still be rejected due to replay/ID uniqueness). Includes a second identity control to confirm connector still works.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML Assertion/@ID must be globally one-time; even if an earlier attempt with that ID failed (e.g., expired), the same ID must not later be accepted in a valid time window (no replay-cache state confusion).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Expired SAML assertion was accepted; NotOnOrAfter was not enforced (freshness failure).
SAML Assertion/@ID reuse was accepted after a prior failed attempt with the same ID; replay/uniqueness tracking is broken or state-confused.
Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute failures to freshness enforcement vs broken SAML setup.

description: Cross-session splicing attempt: start two SP-initiated auth flows (two RelayState/state contexts) and try to complete flow-A using a SAMLResponse bound to flow-B (InResponseTo mismatch). Must be rejected to preserve flow coherence.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: SAML callback must be bound to the correct SP-initiated session context (RelayState/InResponseTo). A SAMLResponse generated for a different auth initiation must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse using a RelayState from a different SP-initiated flow (cross-session splicing / InResponseTo mismatch not enforced).
Dex produced a valid downstream session/identity after a spliced SAML callback, indicating flow coherence failure.

description: Connector mix-up attempt: initiate auth with SAML connector but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback path (mock). Must be rejected; otherwise callback routing is not bound to the initiated connector.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The initiated connector_id must be bound to the callback endpoint. A SAMLResponse for one connector must not be accepted on another connector's callback.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse on the wrong connector callback endpoint, indicating connector/session binding confusion.
Dex issued a downstream identity/session after a SAMLResponse was posted to the wrong connector callback, violating flow coherence.

description: Mid-flight connector reconfiguration: initiate SP flow, then re-provision the SAML connector (e.g., change ssoIssuer) before posting the SAMLResponse. The in-flight response should be rejected; accepting it suggests stale state or non-atomic flow binding across config changes.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authentication flow must be atomic and evaluated under the current connector configuration. An in-flight SAMLResponse should not be accepted if connector verification policy changed after initiation.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an in-flight SAMLResponse after the connector's verification policy (ssoIssuer) changed, indicating non-atomic flow binding or stale validation context.
Dex issued a downstream identity/session even though the connector policy changed mid-flow, violating flow coherence.

description: Auth-code injection across flows: obtain an auth code from one SAML login, then attempt to exchange it using a mismatched redirect_uri to test binding of code to the original authorization request parameters.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the initiating request context (including redirect_uri) and must not be exchangeable under a different redirect_uri or spliced into another client session context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex exchanged an authorization code with a mismatched redirect_uri, indicating auth-code flow context is not coherently bound (possible code injection/splicing).

description: In-flight flow invalidation: start SP-initiated flow, then revoke the session/token context (if any) and attempt to complete the SAML callback using the original RelayState to see if the flow remains valid when it should be invalidated.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Multi-step auth should be atomic; revocation/termination should invalidate any in-flight authentication context so it cannot be completed later (no step skipping or stale state completion).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed completion of an in-flight SAML auth flow after an explicit revocation/termination action, suggesting non-atomic flow handling or stale state acceptance.

description: Cross-client flow splicing: start two SP-initiated auth requests with different client_id values, then attempt to complete client-A's flow using client-B's RelayState (state) to test binding of callback to the initiating client/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: SAML callback completion must be bound to the initiating OAuth client/session (RelayState/state). A RelayState from a different client flow must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SAML callback accepted a RelayState/state from a different client flow (cross-client splicing), violating flow coherence.

description: Duplicate callback completion: complete a single SP-initiated SAML flow, then POST the same SAMLResponse again with the same RelayState to test atomicity (no double-consume of the same flow context).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A single SP-initiated flow context (RelayState/InResponseTo) must be consumed at most once; a second callback for the same flow must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Second SAML callback for the same SP-initiated flow context was accepted (double-consume), violating flow atomicity/order.
Control SAML callback failed; cannot distinguish flow-coherence enforcement from broken SAML setup.

description: In-flight policy flip: initiate SP flow, then reconfigure the SAML connector to enforce signature validation (disable insecureSkipSignatureValidation). Attempt to complete the in-flight flow with attacker-signed assertion; must be rejected if the flow is bound to current connector policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: In-flight authentication must be coherent with current connector configuration; a mid-flight change to stricter validation must not allow completion under stale/previous policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: In-flight SAML flow completed successfully using attacker-signed assertion after connector was tightened, indicating stale policy binding / non-atomic flow coherence.
Post-flip control login failed; cannot distinguish correct rejection from broken connector configuration.

description: Attempt flow-coherence break by swapping RelayState between two concurrent SP-initiated SAML auth flows, then exchanging the resulting auth code and verifying identity binding. This targets session/flow context splicing at the SAML callback boundary.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A SAMLResponse must only complete the exact SP-initiated flow it corresponds to; swapping RelayState/state between flows must be rejected (no cross-session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Flow coherence broken: victim SAMLResponse was accepted when posted with attacker RelayState (cross-flow splicing should be rejected).
Flow coherence broken: attacker SAMLResponse was accepted when posted with victim RelayState (cross-flow splicing should be rejected).
Flow coherence broken: a downstream session/identity was created (or userinfo succeeded) despite RelayState-spliced SAML callback.
Flow coherence broken: a downstream session/identity was created (or userinfo succeeded) despite RelayState-spliced SAML callback.

description: Case confusion in SAML NameID: 'Admin' vs 'admin' should map to different downstream subjects; test for unintended case-folding collision.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals differing only by case in NameID must not collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant NameIDs ('Admin' vs 'admin') collapsed to the same downstream identity (unexpected case-folding collision)

description: Cross-protocol identity merge probe: obtain a baseline identity via password grant, then authenticate via SAML with a different NameID but the same email. Ensure Dex does not collapse these security-distinct principals into one downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A local/password principal and a SAML principal with the same email but different unique identifiers (NameID) must not map to the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
SAML principal with different NameID but same email collapsed into existing downstream subject (email-based account linking/collision)

description: Empty/blank NameID collision probe: authenticate once with a normal NameID and once with an empty NameID. Ensure Dex does not map empty NameID to a shared/previous identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A SAML assertion with an empty NameID must not be mapped to an existing downstream subject (no defaulting/collapsing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty NameID mapped to an existing downstream subject (defaulting/collision on blank identifier)

description: SAML assertion missing <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds) should be rejected; if accepted, broker may grant permissions without upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not accept SAML assertions lacking Conditions (no AudienceRestriction / time bounds), because that would allow permissions beyond UpstreamIntent(auth_context) ∩ BrokerPolicy(config).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion without <Conditions>, allowing authentication/permissions without upstream audience/time constraints (authorization binding failure).
Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish Conditions enforcement from generic SAML misconfiguration.

description: Connector configured with allowedGroups+filterGroups should not emit or effectively grant permissions based on non-allowed groups; test for over-grant via extra groups in assertion.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: When allowedGroups is configured, Dex must not grant or propagate authorization-relevant group claims beyond BrokerPolicy(config); extra upstream groups must not expand effective permissions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker login unexpectedly failed; cannot evaluate whether extra groups cause over-grant vs. normal authn gating.

oracle_checks.assertion: "admins" not in user_group_attacker_meta AND "superusers" not in user_group_attacker_meta
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex propagated non-allowed groups despite filterGroups=true, enabling potential authorization escalation beyond BrokerPolicy(config).

description: SAML connector configured with allowedGroups should deny authentication when user lacks allowed group; attempt login with disallowed group to detect authz-gate bypass (over-grant).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed BrokerPolicy(config); if allowedGroups is configured, users without any allowed group must not be authenticated (no session/permissions granted).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login with allowed group failed; cannot evaluate allowedGroups authorization binding.
Connector accepted SAML login for user lacking any allowedGroups membership, potentially granting permissions beyond BrokerPolicy(config).

description: Config change + re-auth: first enforce CA-based signature validation (attacker-signed should fail), then toggle insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true and show attacker-signed succeeds (demonstrates policy dependence and detects accidental insecure default/override).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: BrokerPolicy(config) must enforce signature validation when configured; attacker-signed assertions must not yield an authenticated session/permissions under the secure configuration.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Under CA-based signature validation, Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAML assertion, granting a session/permissions beyond BrokerPolicy(config).
Even with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true, attacker-signed assertion was rejected; indicates test harness mismatch (not an I5 finding).

description: I5 attack: Config change + re-auth — switch entityIssuer (expected audience) and test whether Dex continues accepting assertions scoped to the old audience (audience source confusion).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: AudienceRestriction must be enforced against the currently configured expected audience (entityIssuer when set). After config change, assertions for the old audience must not be accepted, preventing over-grant across relying-party contexts.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login for audience v1 failed; cannot distinguish audience enforcement from broken SAML setup.
Dex accepted an assertion scoped to the old audience after entityIssuer changed, indicating audience-binding confusion that could over-grant across relying-party contexts.
